FINDING_ID: F001  
SEVERITY: 0.99  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.20  
DESCRIPTION: The artifact as shown is syntactically invalid Python in the Role Assignment area. Multiple class docstrings are unterminated or contain method signatures inside the docstring block without proper closure/indentation, e.g. `DynamicManagementConfig`, `CapabilityFingerprint`, and others. `class ModelSpec:` appears before the preceding docstring is closed. This prevents import, execution, and any runtime validation of the area.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Restore valid class definitions with properly closed triple-quoted docstrings and actual method bodies or `...`/`pass` placeholders. Ensure every class header is followed by an indented suite. Run `python -m py_compile dynamic_management.py`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F002  
SEVERITY: 0.97  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.25  
DESCRIPTION: `RoleAssignment` is used as a dataclass-like value object with fields (`role_map`, `capability_scores`, `pm_model_id`, `_config`, `_models`, `_failure_history`) and is instantiated via `return cls(...)`, but the class declaration shown is not decorated with `@dataclass` and defines no `__init__`. As written, `RoleAssignment.assign()` will raise `TypeError: RoleAssignment() takes no arguments`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `@dataclass` above `class RoleAssignment` or implement an explicit `__init__` matching the constructed fields. Add a unit test for `RoleAssignment.assign([...], cfg)`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F003  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.20  
DESCRIPTION: `ModelSpec` is instantiated in this area (`ModelSpec(...)`) and its attributes are read (`model_id`, `fingerprint`, `tau`, `L`, `c`, `L_std`), but in the provided artifact section it has no actual definition—only a skeletal class header. In isolation, all Role Assignment logic depending on `ModelSpec` construction/access is non-executable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Provide the concrete `ModelSpec` dataclass/class definition in this module section or import it from another module. At minimum, define the fields actually used by this area.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F004  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.20  
DESCRIPTION: `CapabilityFingerprint` methods `as_array()` and `as_normalised_array()` are invoked by Role Assignment, but only skeletal signatures are present in the artifact. The area therefore cannot compute any score or normalization as shown.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Implement `CapabilityFingerprint` concretely, including field definitions (`D_decay`, `v_bar`, `A`, `C`) and both methods. Add direct tests for normalization behavior, especially `D_decay` inversion.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F005  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` can demote the locked PM from the active role map when `active_models` excludes `self.pm_model_id`. The method always seeds `new_map` with `{self.pm_model_id: Role.PM}`, but if `remaining_ids` is empty it returns only that map; otherwise it may return a map containing PM plus active participants. This creates an inconsistent state where `role_map` may include inactive PM or may consist solely of inactive PM if all active models exclude PM. That conflicts with the notion of `active_models` and with “PM static for run duration” if the PM is unavailable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Enforce invariant that the PM must be active to reassign, or explicitly model PM-unavailable as an error/abort state. If `active_models` excludes PM, raise `ValueError` or trigger failure handling rather than silently returning a map containing an inactive PM.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F006  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.45  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` bases `active_models` default on `self.role_map.keys()` rather than the full model universe. If a prior reassignment ever produced a reduced map due to transient inactivity, later calls with `active_models=None` permanently forget models absent from the current role map, even though they still exist in `self._models` and `_failure_history`. This makes liveness restoration impossible by default.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Default `active_models` to `{m.model_id for m in self._models}`. Maintain a separate active-set state if necessary; do not infer system membership from the current role map.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F007  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.40  
DESCRIPTION: `get_ordering()` returns rankings from `self.capability_scores`, but `capability_scores` is only computed at initial assignment and is never updated during `reassign()`, even when `live_fingerprints` are supplied and failure-history penalties alter effective suitability. The returned ordering becomes stale and can materially misrepresent the current capability ordering ≽_rho.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Recompute and store updated scores during `reassign()`, or make `get_ordering()` compute from current state/live inputs instead of frozen initial values. Distinguish raw capability score from adjusted assignment score if both are needed.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F008  
SEVERITY: 0.78  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.50  
DESCRIPTION: COL selection in `reassign()` does not apply the documented deterministic tie-breaking rule. It uses `best_col_id = max(col_scores, key=lambda mid: col_scores[mid])`, so ties depend on dictionary insertion order derived from set iteration over `active_models`, which is not a stable semantic tie-break criterion. This violates the stated plan requirement for deterministic tie-breaking.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Select COL using a composite key `(adjusted_score, tie_break_key(model))` with a deterministic source ordering, as in initial PM assignment. Avoid iterating from an unordered set without sorting.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F009  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35  
DESCRIPTION: `remaining_ids` in `reassign()` is derived from a `set`, so subsequent role assignment order for PAR entries is nondeterministic. While the final mapping is semantically similar, any downstream serialization, snapshot comparison, or reproducibility check may vary run-to-run. In a deterministic management layer, this is undesirable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Sort `remaining_ids` deterministically, e.g. `sorted(mid for mid in active_models if mid != self.pm_model_id)`.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F010  
SEVERITY: 0.72  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.40  
DESCRIPTION: The rule for whether a COL should exist during reassignment uses `if len(self._models) >= 3:` rather than the active model count. If the system started with 3+ models but only 2 are currently active (PM + one other), the code still attempts to assign a COL to the one remaining active non-PM model. That may violate the stated initial rule “Assign COL (if K >= 3)” if K refers to current active pool rather than original pool.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Clarify whether the threshold is based on total configured models or active models. If operationally it should reflect active capacity, change to `if len(active_models) >= 3:` or equivalent.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F011  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.55  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` does not validate uniqueness of `model_id`. Duplicate IDs cause score entries and role assignments to overwrite each other silently because dictionaries are keyed by `model_id`. This can reduce the effective model count, corrupt tie-breaking, and invalidate the PM/COL/PAR mapping.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate that all `model_id` values are unique before scoring. Raise `ValueError` on duplicates.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F012  
SEVERITY: 0.66  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.45  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` silently ignores `active_models` entries not found in `self._models`. Those IDs remain in `remaining_ids`, but since no matching `ModelSpec` is found they are skipped in scoring and disappear from `new_map` without warning. This masks caller errors and can desynchronize manager state.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate `active_models` against known model IDs and raise on unknown entries, or explicitly log/warn and remove them before proceeding.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F013  
SEVERITY: 0.62  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.50  
DESCRIPTION: The failure-history penalty `adjusted = base_score * (1.0 - phi_hist)` uses the lifetime mean over all recorded rounds. This creates path dependence with no decay: an early bad phase can permanently suppress a model even after sustained recovery. Given the comments about persistence windows and dynamic reassignment, this may be too rigid and can prevent the role layer from adapting to current performance.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use a rolling window, exponential decay, or configurable persistence horizon for `phi_hist`. Align with the stated “persistence window for underperformance” if that was intended in this area.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F014  
SEVERITY: 0.60  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60  
DESCRIPTION: There is no invariant validation on role map cardinality or role uniqueness after assignment/reassignment. The intended structure appears to be exactly one PM, at most one COL, and all others PAR, but no internal checker enforces this. Bugs elsewhere could mutate `role_map` into an invalid state undetected.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add a private invariant check method invoked after `assign()` and `reassign()` verifying: PM exists and matches `pm_model_id`, PM count is 1, COL count ≤ 1, all known active models have a role, and all roles are valid.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F015  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.30  
DESCRIPTION: `_capability_score()` docstring claims the return is in `[0, 1]`, but that is only true if `q_tilde` components are each in `[0,1]`, alpha weights are nonnegative, and alpha sums are bounded appropriately. None of those conditions are enforced in the shown area. The documentation overstates a property that may not hold.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either enforce the necessary config/fingerprint constraints in `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__`/`CapabilityFingerprint`, or weaken the docstring to state the range is conditional on validated normalized inputs and weights.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F016  
SEVERITY: 0.55  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.25  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_homogeneous()` docstring says “tie-breaking assigns PM,” but the implementation only checks that one PM exists and all PM scores are equal. It does not verify any specific tie-break behavior or deterministic winner selection. The validator name/docstring and implementation do not match.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either update the validator to assert the expected winner under the specified lexicographic tie-break, or revise the docstring to reflect the weaker property actually tested.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F017  
SEVERITY: 0.52  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.40  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_homogeneous()` does not validate the `k >= 1` precondition. For `k=0`, it constructs an empty model list and then calls `assign()`, which raises `ValueError`. A validator should either reject invalid input explicitly or define its behavior.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add `if k < 1: return False` or raise a documented `ValueError` with a clear message.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F018  
SEVERITY: 0.49  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.20  
DESCRIPTION: `record_failure()` docstring says “Record whether a model failed in the current round,” but the API has no round index and appends blindly. Multiple calls in one round or out-of-order calls will distort the rate. The contract is under-specified relative to the stored structure.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Include `round_idx` in the API or document the required calling discipline clearly. Consider storing `{round_idx: failed}` to prevent duplicate appends for one round.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F019  
SEVERITY: 0.47  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35  
DESCRIPTION: `validate_k1()` and `validate_homogeneous()` depend on `ModelSpec` constructor shorthand forms (`ModelSpec("m1", ...)`, `ModelSpec(f"m{i}", fp)`), while `reassign()` later constructs `ModelSpec` with additional named parameters (`tau`, `L`, `c`, `L_std`). This suggests inconsistent constructor assumptions across the same area and increases risk of validator/runtime mismatch.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Standardize `ModelSpec` construction with explicit fields and defaults. Use the same constructor style across tests and production code.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F020  
SEVERITY: 0.43  
FLAW_CLASS: 7  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.25  
DESCRIPTION: `reassign()` performs a linear search `next((m for m in models_for_scoring if m.model_id == mid), None)` for each active model, making lookup O(n²) in the number of models. This is unnecessary overhead in a component that may run every round.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Build a dictionary once, e.g. `model_by_id = {m.model_id: m for m in models_for_scoring}`, and do O(1) lookups.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F021  
SEVERITY: 0.41  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35  
DESCRIPTION: The comments say “PM selected by argmax with deterministic tie-breaking” and “COL/PAR dynamic between rounds,” but there is no explicit documentation of how ties in reassignment interact with hysteresis and failure penalties. This leaves an important policy edge case ambiguous.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document the exact reassignment ordering: adjusted score first, then hysteresis check, then deterministic tie-break. Include examples for exact-tie and within-epsilon cases.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F022  
SEVERITY: 0.39  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.30  
DESCRIPTION: `get_failure_history_rate()` and reassignment logic assume every appended history element is boolean, but `record_failure()` does not validate `failed` type. Non-bool truthy/falsy values will be summed numerically and may corrupt rates silently.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Type-check `failed` at runtime or coerce via `bool(failed)` and document that behavior.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F023  
SEVERITY: 0.36  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.20  
DESCRIPTION: The module imports many unused symbols in this area (`math`, `time`, `warnings`, `Callable`, `ClassVar`, `FrozenSet`, `Literal`, `Protocol`, `Union`, `logging`, etc.). While some may be for other areas, in the provided area this obscures actual dependencies and weakens maintainability.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Scope imports to used symbols per module or split areas into separate modules. Run a linter such as Ruff/Flake8 to remove unused imports.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: F024  
SEVERITY: 0.34  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.45  
DESCRIPTION: There is no explicit check that `config.get_alpha(role)` returns a 4-vector matching the fingerprint dimensionality. If it returns the wrong shape, `np.dot` may error or produce unintended results depending on array shapes. The role layer assumes this invariant but does not defend it.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Validate alpha vector shape in `_capability_score()` or in `DynamicManagementConfig.__post_init__`. Raise a clear exception on mismatch.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F025  
SEVERITY: 0.33  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.45  
DESCRIPTION: `_compute_pool_max()` returns zeros for an empty input, which is sensible locally, but `reassign()` can pass an empty active-model list if `active_models` excludes all known non-PM models and PM handling changes later. The correctness then depends on downstream normalization behavior inside `as_normalised_array()`, which is not asserted here.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Explicitly guard empty scoring pools and document the expected normalization semantics for zero maxima.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F026  
SEVERITY: 0.31  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.20  
DESCRIPTION: The example in `RoleAssignment` docstring presumes a default-constructible `DynamicManagementConfig()` with valid alpha vectors and baselines, but the class definition shown does not establish defaults. The example may be non-runnable.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Ensure `DynamicManagementConfig` has usable defaults or change examples to construct it explicitly with required parameters.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F027  
SEVERITY: 0.29  
FLAW_CLASS: 6  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.30  
DESCRIPTION: `record_failure()` will create history for any arbitrary `model_id`, including unknown models never present in `_models`. This can pollute internal state and create misleading rates.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Reject unknown model IDs unless dynamic pool membership is explicitly supported. If supported, update `_models` and related structures consistently.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F028  
SEVERITY: 0.27  
FLAW_CLASS: 1  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35  
DESCRIPTION: The initial PM selection uses deterministic tie-breaking, but COL assignment in `assign()` can choose a model with lower global suitability than another because PM is chosen solely by PM score and then removed before COL optimization. If the intended objective is joint role-optimality across PM and COL, this greedy decomposition may be suboptimal.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Clarify whether the converged plan intends greedy sequential assignment or joint optimization over role assignments. If joint optimality matters, evaluate all PM/COL pairings and choose the best under the formal objective.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F029  
SEVERITY: 0.25  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.15  
DESCRIPTION: The comment `# Player Manager — static for run duration (HARD)` encodes an important invariant only in comments. There is no public API contract or exception behavior documented for attempts to violate it during reassignment.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Promote this to an explicit invariant in method docstrings and enforce it with checks/errors where relevant.  
VERIFIED: FALSE

FINDING_ID: F030  
SEVERITY: 0.24  
FLAW_CLASS: 7  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.20  
DESCRIPTION: `assign()` fully sorts candidate lists to obtain the maximum PM and COL, which is O(n log n); only the top element is needed. This is a minor inefficiency.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use `max()` with a composite key for PM/COL selection; sort only if a full ordering is required.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: the most serious issues are the area’s non-executable state as shown (F001–F004), stale/non-deterministic reassignment behavior (F007–F009), and missing input/invariant validation around model identity and active-set semantics (F005, F006, F011, F012).
